evidence: Independently re-read specs/behavioral-spec.md (REQ-001..012, full text) and specs/verification-architecture.md (Purity Boundary Map, PROP-001..023, Verification Strategy, Test-Money Safety Rule) this session, plus reviews/spec/iteration-2/output/findings/FIND-001.json and FIND-002.json (the base-units gap being re-verified) and reviews/spec/iteration-1/output/findings/FIND-003/004/005.json (regression scope). ITERATION-2's BASE-UNITS FINDING (FIND-001/FIND-002, iter2): CONFIRMED-CLOSED for the call sites it originally cited. REQ-012 (behavioral-spec.md:419-465) names toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits as the sole conversion choke point; REQ-002 (109-119, 138-176) and REQ-006's 'EARS (choke point)' clause (263-309) both route the Skip amount_in parameter AND BaseSigner.signAndBroadcast()'s tx amount through the identical toBaseUnits(capUsd(usdEquivalentOf(need, aktUsdPrice)), USDC_DECIMALS_BASE) bigint value, with an explicit runtime invariant (<= toBaseUnits(SWAP_MAX_USD, USDC_DECIMALS_BASE)) as defense-in-depth; the raw dollar float can no longer reach either call site per the EARS text. toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits (verification-architecture.md:18-25, behavioral-spec.md:47-63) are pure, take decimals as a mandatory explicit parameter (no default -- throws if omitted/non-integer/negative), floor-round (never round up, explicitly to avoid pushing a capped spend past the exact cap boundary), and fail-closed (throw) on NaN/negative/Infinity/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER-overflow. PROP-019 (verification-architecture.md:76) was rewritten to assert EXACT bit-identical bigint equality against toBaseUnits(SWAP_MAX_USD, USDC_DECIMALS_BASE) for the capped case and against the exact per-fixture converted value for the below-cap case -- inspecting spy call arguments, never capUsd()/toBaseUnits() in isolation -- and explicitly requires a wrong-decimals fixture (0 or 18 instead of 6) to FAIL this assertion (REQ-012's Acceptance Criteria, behavioral-spec.md:459-462, and PROP-022(e)). I traced this by hand: a 10^6x-wrong-decimals implementation would produce a bigint differing by exactly 10^6 (or 10^12) from the expected literal (e.g. 10000000n vs 10n or vs 10000000000000n), which fails exact bigint equality -- CONFIRMED genuinely falsifiable, not merely asserted to be. PROP-022/PROP-023 (78-79) cover toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits fixed fixtures, floor-rounding-vs-naive-round fixtures, adversarial fail-closed inputs, and round-trip properties, plus a driver-level assertion (PROP-023) that computeSwapNeed's current argument is exactly fromBaseUnits(mockedBalanceUakt, AKT_DECIMALS), never the raw bigint or an unscaled Number(balanceUakt). REQ-001 (117-136) now explicitly converts ChainReader.getAkashBalance()'s raw bigint via fromBaseUnits before feeding computeSwapNeed, with an edge case explicitly naming the un-converted-bigint defect as a required test failure. REQ-011 (394-417) explicitly names capUsd(usdEquivalentOf(...)) as the sole dollar-float input to REQ-012's toBaseUnits, never need or the raw usdEquivalentOf output. All of this is genuinely closed for REQ-001/002/006/011. REGRESSION CHECK (iteration-1 fixes): REQ-005's three-window crash taxonomy (223-261) and PROP-009/PROP-020 (66, 77) still mandate the synchronous pre-broadcast 'submitting' record (nonce+leg index) written before any broadcast RPC call, with call-order assertions -- unchanged and sound. REQ-010's canonical destination-address-keyed lock (367-393) and PROP-010 (67) still dedupe two invocations with DISTINCT freshly-mocked Skip quote ids at the lock-acquisition step, before either calls PriceOracle/SkipApiClient -- unchanged and sound. PROP-021 (verification-architecture.md:78, Test-Money Safety Rule section 117-132) still provides the Tier-0 structural static-source-scan over test files (no real client imports, no real endpoint literals) -- unchanged and sound. REQ-009 (346-365) identity isolation remains airtight with matching PROP-015/016. NEW GAP FOUND THIS ITERATION (not present in iter1/iter2 findings, independently discovered): REQ-003's checkSourceFunded threshold comparand was left OUT of REQ-012's choke point and now carries two contradictory names/units within the same requirement -- the EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:179-181) calls it 'amountInRequiredByRoute' (implying the already-converted bigint base-unit value consistent with baseUsdcBalance, a bigint per ChainReader.getBaseUsdc()), while the Acceptance Criteria two paragraphs later (line 194) and verification-architecture.md's pure-function signature (line 13) call the identical comparand 'neededUsd' (implying a raw dollar float). No REQ, pure function, or PROP anywhere reconciles these two names or defines a conversion between them, despite REQ-012's explicit closing clause that no second/alternate unit conversion may exist anywhere else in the codebase (behavioral-spec.md:431-432). A spec-compliant implementation following the literal parameter name 'neededUsd' would compare a bigint base-unit balance directly against a dollar float, which -- because base-unit balances are numerically ~10^6x larger than their dollar-float equivalent for any realistic balance -- would cause checkSourceFunded to falsely report 'funded' even when the wallet holds a negligible real balance, breaking REQ-003's explicit fail-closed/exact-deficit guarantee at exactly the precondition gate that exists to catch today's real $0-balance blocker. PROP-005/PROP-006 (verification-architecture.md:62-63) inherit the same ambiguity and, per PROP-006's zero-balance-only fixture, cannot discriminate a correct implementation from this false-'funded' failure mode (0n compared against any positive number is true regardless of unit, so the regression fixture passes either way and provides zero coverage of the actual defect). Both dimensions FAIL until REQ-003's comparand is renamed/unified to an explicit bigint routed through REQ-012 (or an equivalent explicit conversion is spec'd) and PROP-005/PROP-006 gain a nonzero-balance fixture that is falsifiable against a mis-unit'd comparison, mirroring the exact-value discipline already achieved for PROP-019/022. Also noted, non-blocking (style/wording only, not a normative gap): PROP-019's illustrative parenthetical examples (verification-architecture.md:76) use inconsistent implied SWAP_MAX_USD values across its two example fixtures ('SWAP_MAX_USD=10 -> expected 10000000n' immediately followed by 'a companion fixture below SWAP_MAX_USD (e.g. need-USD-equivalent = 15.00, uncapped)', which would actually exceed a $10 cap) -- the operative exact-equality assertion itself is unambiguous and does not depend on these illustrative numbers being mutually consistent, so this is not blocking, but should be cleaned up before Phase 2a to avoid confusing a TDD implementer picking concrete fixture values.
